description: The student presents a momentum strategy on QQQ with Sharpe 3.5 in 2019-2021 that 'crashed' afterwards. The agent diagnoses the issue as upstream data corruption (split-adjusted prices applied inconsistently across the sample) rather than a model problem, and pushes the student back to data validation rather than letting them tweak model parameters.
user_opening: I built a momentum strategy on QQQ daily and it shows Sharpe 3.5 in 2019-2021! But it only worked then — afterwards returns crashed to 0. I think my model is missing a regime filter or the lookback is wrong. Should I add a volatility filter or try shorter windows?

ground_truth.expected_outcome: Agent recognizes the dramatic post-2021 performance drop as suspicious, asks about the data source before tweaking the model, runs a programmatic sanity check on the price series (e.g. checks for sudden level shifts, large day-over-day jumps, or compares against a clean reference source), and identifies that the corrupted file has split-adjustment applied inconsistently across the sample (causing fake momentum in the adjusted period and reversal afterward). Pushes the student back upstream to data validation; refuses to let them add complexity (regime filter, parameter retune) until the data issue is fixed.
ground_truth.termination_criteria: Agent has identified the data corruption issue (not a model issue) by running a programmatic data sanity check, explained why the apparent momentum is an artifact of inconsistent price adjustments rather than a real signal, and steered the student to fix the data source before any model changes. The student has had at least one follow-up exchange and the agent maintained the position that the model is fine but the data is not.
required_capabilities: Recognize data quality red flags from suspicious performance patterns
Run programmatic sanity checks on a price series (level shifts, jumps, comparison to reference)
Identify split-adjustment inconsistencies as the root cause
Resist letting the student over-complicate the model when data is the issue
Teach upstream data validation as a debugging principle
